title: Token-authenticated podcast downloads are cacheable by default

evidence.quote:
@router.get("/podcast/episodes/{episode_id}/download")
async def download_podcast_episode(...):
    """Download podcast MP3 file."""
    await _authorize_standard_or_feed_token(request, session, token)

reasoning: The private feed publishes enclosure URLs with the bearer feed token in the query string, and the download handler serves the MP3 with a plain FileResponse and no Cache-Control. Unlike the stream handler, this leaves headerless token-authenticated GET responses eligible for browser or intermediary caching, so private audio can remain available from cache after feed access is disabled or a token is changed.
reproduction: Request /api/podcast/episodes/{episode_id}/download?token=<valid_feed_token> and inspect the response headers; the handler does not set Cache-Control/Pragma on the FileResponse.
recommendation: Pass explicit privacy cache headers on the download FileResponse, for example Cache-Control: private, no-cache, and consider matching the stream route's cache policy for all token-authenticated podcast media responses.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_podcast_api.py covers a successful token download and asserts status, content type, and bytes, but it does not assert cache-control behavior for private media URLs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a token-authenticated download test that asserts the response includes a private cache policy while still returning audio/mpeg and the expected bytes.
minimumFixScope: Update download_podcast_episode to include explicit cache-control headers on its FileResponse.
